name: Art Nouveau
garments: flowing, corset-free "reform dress" promoted alongside the style, though rarely adopted at scale
reacts_against: historicism — the 19th century's habit of reviving past styles wholesale — by inventing an explicitly new decorative language based on plant and flower forms.
revivals: a visible influence on 1960s psychedelic poster art's flowing linework

wiki_facts.other_names: Modern Style (Britain)Glasgow Style (Scotland)Jugendstil (Germany)Stile Liberty (Italy)Modernismo (Spain)Modernisme (Catalonia)Wiener Jugendstil or Secessionsstil (Austro-Hungary)Nieuwe Kunst (the Netherlands)Arte Nova (Portugal)Arta 1900 (Romania)Tiffany Style (US)
wiki_facts.key_motifs: "Whiplash" curves, sinuous lines, stylized natural forms (flowers, insects, vines), female figures, peacock feathers
wiki_facts.key_colours: Muted palettes including olive green, mustard yellow, brown, lilac, and sage, often with accents of gold and silver
wiki_facts.key_values: Integration of fine and applied arts, rejection of historicism, ornamentation based on nature, use of modern materials

findings: mostly muted — about 64% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from the Aesthetics Wiki images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
